h1: El Paso County Justice of the Peace Court Ticket Lawyer
intro: If a Sheriff's deputy, a DPS trooper or a constable wrote your ticket in El Paso County, the case is in one of the county's Justice of the Peace precincts, not at Municipal Court downtown. Attorney Robert Navar appears in every JP office for a flat $69 per citation.
summaryHeading: Sheriff, DPS or constable ticket? It is in a Justice of the Peace court
summary: El Paso County says it directly: a citation "issued in El Paso County by an agency OTHER THAN the El Paso Police Department" is handled by the Justice of the Peace precinct office noted on your citation by the officer.

The county lists eight JP offices: Precincts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6-1, 6-2 and 7, spread from downtown and the Northeast to George Dieter, Socorro Rd, Clint, far-east El Paso and Vinton. The precinct number on the ticket tells you which one.

JP courts hear Class C traffic cases with fines that, by the county's description, do not exceed $500; the amount in any case is set by the court. Paying the ticket enters a plea and results in a conviction.
Our flat fee in any JP precinct is $69 per citation, with discounted add-ons for extra tickets from the same stop. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: How to Tell Your Ticket Is in a JP Court, and Which Precinct
paragraphs: Two lines on the citation answer the question. The first is the issuing agency. The El Paso County Sheriff's Office patrols the unincorporated parts of the county, such as Montana Vista, the Upper Valley and Canutillo, and stretches of Montana Ave and Loop 375 outside the city limits. DPS troopers work I-10, US-54 and the highways toward Fabens and Tornillo. County constables write citations in their own precincts. None of them file at El Paso Municipal Court; the county's instruction for any citation "by an agency OTHER THAN the El Paso Police Department" is to contact the JP precinct office noted on the ticket.

The second line is the precinct itself. The officer writes the JP precinct (or the court name and address) on the citation, and that is where the case is docketed, regardless of where you live. A Northeast resident ticketed by a trooper on I-10 near Anthony has a case in Vinton, not on Dyer St. If the precinct line is blank or illegible, our free ticket and warrant lookup will find it.

sections.heading: What the County Says a JP Court Can Do
paragraphs: The county describes each justice of the peace as an elected judge with original jurisdiction in criminal cases where the fine does not exceed $500, plus civil cases up to $10,000, and the authority to issue arrest warrants. For a traffic ticket that means the judge who hears your case is the one who can sign a warrant if the appearance date passes, the fine is set by that court within the legal range, and, as the precinct pages note, clerks cannot give legal advice or provide legal forms.

Several precinct pages add practical details: payments are taken in cash, money order, cashier's check and card (a convenience fee may apply), criminal payment plans are set up only after a hearing and judgment, and some offices ask for contact in person or by email because phone access is limited. A missed JP appearance date can produce a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge, and in general an unresolved case can be reported to the state's Failure to Appear program, which blocks a DPS license renewal until the court clears it.

sections.heading: Why Trooper and Deputy Tickets Play Differently Than City Tickets
paragraphs: A large share of JP traffic cases come from DPS troopers, and trooper tickets have their own pattern. Troopers write for higher speeds on the interstate, so citations for 25 mph or more over the limit are common, a speed many courts will not resolve with a driving safety course. They also write no insurance and expired registration tickets on US-54 and I-10. Troopers are reassigned around the state, and an officer who cannot be produced for trial is a legitimate reason to ask for a dismissal.

Commercial drivers need a different plan. I-10 trooper tickets frequently involve CDL holders, and Texas law does not allow a court to use deferred disposition or a driving safety course for a CDL holder's traffic offense. For those clients we concentrate on defects in the citation and on negotiating a charge that does not count as a serious violation under the commercial rules. Tell us at intake if you hold a CDL.

sections.heading: How We Handle a JP Case for $69
paragraphs: We file a notice of appearance and a plea of not guilty in the precinct named on your citation before the appearance date. The court sets a pretrial or announcement docket, and Robert Navar or a member of our staff attends and confers with the prosecutor assigned to that precinct. The order of business is the same in every JP office: we look for grounds for an outright dismissal first, then ask for deferred disposition or a course dismissal where the judge allows it, and when neither is offered we ask for a reduced, non-moving charge. Each judge sets the terms of a deferral in that court's discretion, so the request is tailored to the precinct. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances.

The fee is $69 per citation in any El Paso County JP precinct, flat, with no hourly billing and no added charge for a continuance. Extra citations from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons at checkout. If a warrant exists, we add $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one and handle the recall with the ticket. Court costs and any deferral or course fee are set by the court. The consultation is free and se habla español.

faqs.q: How do I know which JP precinct has my ticket?
faqs.a: The officer writes the precinct or the court's name on the citation, and El Paso County directs drivers to the "Justice of the Peace precinct office noted on your citation." If you cannot read it, our free lookup form will identify the court.

faqs.q: Where are the El Paso County JP courts?
faqs.a: The county lists eight offices: Precinct 1 at 424 Executive Center; Precinct 2 at 4641 Cohen Ave. in the Northeast; Precinct 3 at the County Courthouse, 500 E. San Antonio; Precinct 4 at 2350 George Dieter; Precinct 5 at 9521 Socorro Rd.; Precinct 6-1 at 190 N. San Elizario Rd. in Clint; Precinct 6-2 at 14608 Greg Dr.; and Precinct 7 at 435 E. Vinton Rd. in Vinton.

faqs.q: How much is a lawyer for a JP court ticket?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation in any precinct. Additional citations from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons; warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to drive out to the precinct office?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file the appearance and attend the docket for you, whether the precinct is downtown, in Clint or in Vinton. You would appear only if the case were set for trial, which we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: Will a JP judge grant deferred disposition?
faqs.a: Deferred disposition is available to a justice court under Texas law, but it is granted in the judge's discretion and each precinct sets its own terms. High-speed, CDL and repeat cases face more resistance, which is where an attorney's request, with a dismissal argument still on the table, tends to matter.

faqs.q: A trooper ticketed me on I-10 months ago and I forgot. Is there a warrant?
faqs.a: Possibly, and there may be a hold on your license renewal. Call us the same day. We file an appearance, ask the JP court to recall the warrant and put the ticket back on a docket; see traffic warrant recall.
